discovery: Rydberg blockade and programmable arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms for quantum simulation and quantum information

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum optics
motivation: Lukin (with Zoller, Jaksch and co-workers) showed theoretically that the strong dipolar interaction between Rydberg atoms blocks multiple excitation, and that this 'Rydberg blockade' provides a fast, robust entangling mechanism. In 2009 Browaeys (with Grangier) and Saffman (with Walker) independently observed blockade between two single atoms held in optical tweezers, and then made the first Rydberg-mediated entanglement and CNOT gates. From these single-quantum experiments, the three built reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms with controlled interactions. These arrays have become a leading platform for quantum simulation of quantum magnetism, spin liquids and topological phases, and for error-corrected logical qubits. This body of work is a textbook example of patient, controlled experiments on individual quanta, and it turned the interaction physics of Rydberg atoms into a new kind of programmable quantum matter.
